Sudo Nova is a team inspired by Linux, open source, software engineering, data, and AI. We aim to transform scientific challenges into creative, practical solutions for Earth and space. Starting as a solo initiative, we're open to curious collaborators in development, data science, AI/ML, design, and storytelling. Our mission is to learn, innovate, and build something meaningful together.

Root Access to the Universe.
summary:
SurfaceSignal transforms complex satellite radar data into accessible insights about environmental changes on Earth.

Developed by Sudo Nova for the Dancing with the SARs challenge, our platform uses NASA–ISRO NISAR observations to investigate surface changes in Brazil's flood-prone Taquari Valley.

We processed 19 real satellite acquisitions, producing 17 historical comparisons that reveal changes in radar backscatter. These observations are enriched with rainfall estimates, historical surface-water occurrence, land cover, elevation, and regional geographic information.

Through our publicly accessible, bilingual web platform, users can explore interactive 2D/3D maps, compare observations across dates, and understand scientific evidence without specialized technical knowledge.

SurfaceSignal distinguishes observed changes from possible environmental interpretations, making uncertainties and limitations explicit rather than presenting unverified flood detections as facts.

By connecting Earth observation, geospatial processing, environmental context, and inclusive design, SurfaceSignal demonstrates how satellite data can become more understandable and useful for communities, researchers, and local decision-makers.
details:
The Problem

Satellite missions generate extraordinary amounts of environmental information, but interpreting that information often requires specialized knowledge, complex scientific software, and substantial computing resources.

This creates a gap between the availability of Earth observation data and the ability of communities to understand environmental changes affecting their regions.

In flood-prone areas such as Brazil's Taquari Valley, accessible historical observations can support environmental awareness, education, and informed local discussions.

Our Solution

SurfaceSignal — Making Earth's Changes Understandable

SurfaceSignal is a publicly accessible, bilingual platform that transforms satellite radar measurements into interactive geographic visualizations and understandable environmental information.

Our pilot focuses on Lajeado, Estrela, and the surrounding Taquari Valley in southern Brazil.

The platform is available at:

https://surfacesignal.earth

Rather than displaying raw satellite imagery alone, SurfaceSignal connects measured changes with historical observations, complementary environmental datasets, and transparent scientific explanations.

How It Works

1. Satellite Data Acquisition

We use NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) products, discovered through the Alaska Satellite Facility.

Our pilot dataset includes 19 real satellite acquisitions collected between June and October 2026, representing approximately 131 GB of original HDF5 data.

2. Radar Change Detection

Our Python processing pipeline reads selected geographic regions from the radar products, applies validity masks, aligns compatible acquisitions, and calculates temporal differences in radar backscatter.

The resulting 17 comparisons identify increases, decreases, and experimental candidate open-water changes.

3. Environmental Context Integration

Radar changes do not necessarily identify their underlying causes.

To provide additional context, SurfaceSignal integrates complementary environmental information:

  • CHIRPS v3 satellite-based rainfall estimates.
  • JRC Global Surface Water historical occurrence.
  • ESA WorldCover land-cover classifications.
  • Copernicus DEM elevation and terrain information.
  • IBGE geographic boundaries.
  • Brazilian Geological Survey hydrological bulletins.

These datasets help users investigate possible explanations while retaining the distinction between direct measurements, historical references, and unverified hypotheses.

4. Interactive Exploration

The application provides an interactive geographic experience with:

  • 2D maps and optional 3D globe visualization.
  • Historical satellite observation timelines.
  • Before-and-after comparisons.
  • Georeferenced candidate-change layers.
  • Environmental context and source information.
  • Portuguese and English interfaces.
  • Accessibility controls and plain-language scientific explanations.

5. Reproducible Data Publication

The backend generates scientific artifacts, geographic layers, statistics, and evidence records through a deterministic processing workflow.

Prepared outputs are published as versioned JSON and GeoJSON datasets consumed by a statically deployed Next.js application.

This architecture allows visitors to explore historical results without downloading the original 131 GB dataset, running scientific software, or creating an account.

Technology Stack

Backend: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Rasterio, h5py, SciPy, Shapely, PyProj, and ASF Search.

Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and MapLibre GL JS.

Data and Processing: NASA–ISRO NISAR GCOV, HDF5, GeoTIFF, GeoJSON, geospatial transformations, temporal comparison, and scientific provenance records.

Infrastructure: GitHub, automated testing, reproducible static-data publication, and Cloudflare Pages.

Innovation and Accessibility

SurfaceSignal addresses more than the technical challenge of processing radar imagery.

Its central innovation is translating complex Earth observation evidence into an accessible geographic experience.

The interface supports bilingual navigation, adjustable text size, high-contrast presentation, reduced motion, and keyboard-accessible interactions.

We also preserve scientific transparency by identifying data sources, acquisition dates, processing limitations, and the exploratory nature of detected changes.

Impact and Future Potential

SurfaceSignal demonstrates how satellite data can become useful beyond specialized scientific environments.

Its potential applications include environmental education, community awareness, historical change analysis, and supporting evidence-informed discussions by local organizations.

The processing architecture is designed to support additional geographic regions without rewriting the fundamental analysis algorithms.

Future development could incorporate independently validated environmental references, additional satellite missions, and more detailed local planning applications.

Scientific limitations: SurfaceSignal is an exploratory historical analysis platform, not a real-time warning, flood prediction, or emergency response system. Radar changes and candidate water detections require independent validation before being treated as confirmed environmental impacts.

Project Resources

Live Application: https://surfacesignal.earth

Source Code and Technical Documentation: https://github.com/sudo-nova-nsac26/surface_signal

Project Presentation: https://github.com/sudo-nova-nsac26/presentation

Team Portfolio: https://sudonova.surfacesignal.earth

Our GitHub repository contains the project's implementation, scientific methodology, data-processing pipeline, reproducibility instructions, and technical documentation.
